headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: Replit Agent can write broad workspace state while cognee handles personal/finance data and has allowlisted egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A plausible bridge exists because agent_a uses session memory and agent_b reads/writes Repl workspace files. If cognee outputs are copied into the Replit workspace, Replit Agent may treat file content as trusted instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from the profiles.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are placed into Repl workspace files
IF Replit Agent ingests workspace file content as instructions
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of shared files
Prefix imported text with explicit non-instruction markers
Review any file-fed prompts before execution
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches personal data and finance data, while agent_b can read files and has broad network egress plus secrets handling. If cognee material is copied into the Replit workspace, Replit Agent can exfiltrate sensitive content to third-party APIs or deployments. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default Replit workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive cognee outputs are stored in Repl workspace files
IF Replit Agent sends those files or derived context to external APIs
mitigations: Do not place sensitive data in shared Repl files
Restrict Replit egress to approved endpoints
Redact personal and finance data before transfer
Rotate any secrets exposed in workspace files
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can mutate shared state if cognee writes into a workspace that Replit Agent also edits. agent_b explicitly writes files and modifies git state; agent_a has session memory and handles workflows/documents, so concurrent edits can collide. Because no locking or coordination primitive is documented, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF either agent edits files or git state without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Pause one agent during the other's write phase
Commit frequently to reduce conflict windows
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add file and git locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, and agent_b can act on workspace files and git state. If Replit Agent treats cognee output as authoritative, downstream actions may propagate errors. The profiles do not prove automatic execution, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Replit Agent consumes cognee-generated plans without verification
IF those plans are used to edit code or commit changes
mitigations: Require human review before commits
Add a verification checklist for imported plans
Compare outputs against source documents
Limit agent_b to draft-only changes
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a touches personal data and finance data, while agent_b handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl environment. If EU or regulated data from cognee is moved into Replit-managed storage or services, residency and retention obligations may be breached. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data from cognee is transferred into Replit-managed storage
IF the deployment environment lacks a documented DPA or residency control
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Replit workspaces
Document data residency for each dataset
Minimize retention of imported records
Review vendor terms before transfer
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
